title: Pinecone Pricing: Plans and Costs Explained (2026)
summary: Pinecone pricing charges a monthly minimum plus metered storage and operation costs across four plans, helping you estimate your bill.
body_markdown:
## Frequently asked questions


Each answer below was checked against Pinecone's pricing page on 2026-10-31. Plans and rates change, so confirm on that page before you commit.


Pinecone offers a free starter plan, and it's capped on purpose. Hit the caps and you either stop being able to write or query, or you move to a paid plan, where a monthly minimum can apply whether or not you use it.


Look up that minimum before you build on the free tier, not after.


### Does Pinecone charge for deleted or idle vectors?


Idle vectors cost you; deleted ones stop costing storage. You pay to keep data stored even if nobody queries it, and on a paid plan an idle index can still hit the minimum.


The delete itself counts as a write, so wiping a large index in bulk isn't free. Delete in planned batches and check the write bill afterward.


### Can I leave Pinecone without re-embedding my data?


Generally yes, if you can get the vectors back out. An embedding is just a list of numbers produced by your embedding model, and it works in any database that accepts that model's output.


Re-embedding is only forced if you change models or never kept the source text. Keep your original documents and IDs somewhere you control, and test a full export on a small index first.


Fetching vectors back counts as reads, so budget for that too.


### Is Pinecone cheaper than self-hosting a vector database?


It depends on your query pattern and on who maintains the servers. Pinecone charges for reads, writes and storage, and you pay no one to run it. Self-hosting swaps those charges for server costs and engineering hours.


A light, steady workload often favors the managed service. A heavy query load can tip the other way. Price both with your real query volume, including the staff time.


### How do I stop a surprise Pinecone bill?


Estimate your monthly reads and writes before you pick a plan, then compare that to the plan's minimum and limits. After launch, watch usage weekly for the first month, because a new feature or a chatty script can multiply queries.


Use any spending alerts or caps the console offers, and keep a test index separate from production so experiments never run on the paid one.
